profile.headline: Software Engineer at Humanoid/SKL Robotics
profile.summary:
Serial entrepreneur, consultant, engineer.  Have worked with embedded systems, embedded Linux, FPGA based CPU design and small hardware systems. Experience with robot power systems, communication, battery BMS's and charging.  

Started a few Boston area companies.  Have built and run small engineering groups which produced innovative products. Some experience with venture capital and the people around it. Mediocre race car driver (mid-pack).

Specialties: Embedded systems, firmware, embedded Linux, Verilog, CPU simulation, network protocols, routers.  Small system hardware and software design.  Small hardware projects, FPGA's, CPLD's, VHDL, PCB layout, fabrication. Batteries, BMS systems and charging.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Robot firmware, communications, functional safety and systems programming
positions.insights: Skills: Software Infrastructure · functional safety software · C, C++, Python · ARM, AURIX firmware

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Extensive work on robot firmware, motor controllers, BMS, power, display, charging.  Interface between firmware and control software.  Robot power control subsystem.  Firmware simulation and emulation environments.  Test stands for BMS and power system development.   FPGA work for communication.  System software for ARM and AURIX based subsystems. Safety system design and firmware  using Aurix TC3/4 for IEC 61508 compliance.

Created end-to-end safety firmware development/release system using CI, HIL testing, simulation, coverage and static analysis, capable of supporting TUV certification of a robot functional safety system.

I helped take Spot from a prototype to a production robot.  I wrote the battery BMS firmware and power control firmware.  I moved BD's firmware from C to C++ and ported their entire controls stack from X86 to ARM.  I wrote most of the firmware the latest version of Stretch, moving the actuators from CAN to Ethernet.  I wrote simulators for the Stretch safety system and prototyped BD's first functional safety computer.
positions.insights: Skills: C (Programming Language) · Python (Programming Language) · Verilog · C++ · Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA) · Git · Linux

positions.title: Hardware Engineer
positions.description: Emulation of custom CPU and verification of CPU modules using SystemVerilog and UVM.  Automatic code generation and complete UVM test benches from scratch.  Extensive co-simulation of ARM CPU’s (32 and 64 bit) with golden models.  Extensive debugging of issues at RTL and software level.  Bare metal testing of new silicon, porting of existing hypervisors. New flows using embedded C code.  Constrained random (CRV) testing of modules using UVM.

positions.title: Contractor
positions.description: Contractor in virtual machine group working on SMP performance improvements.

positions.title: Engineer
positions.description:
General hardware and software consulting for embedded systems, specializing in Linux. http://www.heeltoe.com

Highlights:

- Altera NIOS-II CPU simulation, instruction set simulator
- Linux ports to OMAP, Davinci ARM cpu's
- X86-64 raw boot, PXE boot, mmu init code
- Re-creation of MIT CADR lisp machine in FPGA
- Co-simulation of custom verilog CPUs with behavioral models
- Multicore MIPS CPU debugging with verilog co-simulation.
- Altera NIOS II CPU simulation with Modelsim
- Xilinx Virtex 4 PPC405 firmware, co-simulation
- CPLD based asynchronous bus interface
- Kernal/FPGA Interaction debugging
- PIC, Atmel, MOT micro-controller software
- USB host controller software & debugging

positions.title: linux consultant
positions.description: Helped bring up linux on a new MIPS processor.  Modifications to linux kernel to support new cpu, mods to SIMH, behavioral and RTL simulations.  Linux booted in simulation.

positions.title: Consultant
positions.description: Brought up linux on custom ARM SDR hardware platform.  Help with booting, hardware debug, file system and basic apps.  System had 5 cpus and an large FPGA. Software defined radio.

positions.title: Engineer
positions.description: TCP/IP routing code for 2000 modem telco box.  The product had 18 blades with at least 3 cpus per blade.  TCP/IP routing, OSPF, fair share queuing, etc... Worked with Brian Del Vecchio to design an innovative scheme which allowed us to describe each of the thousands of internal data items in one place and one place only.  Resulting descriptions "compiled" into html, C header files, cli tables, etc...

positions.title: Co-founder, CTO
positions.description: Large scale servers for IP address management, DNS, DHCP,RADIUS.  At one time used to run Comcast's cable modem network.  Sold to Cisco Systems.

positions.title: Co-founder, CTO
positions.description: Small ISP with dial-up and 56k lines.  Sold to Verio.

positions.title: Founder, Chief Engineer
positions.description: Small botique software company.  Developed and sold a PPP client for the Macintosh as well as OEM routing software including multilink PPP.  Software licensed to DEC, Cisco, Microsoft and many others. Some of FCR's software is in Cisco IOS and Window's NT.

positions.title: Co-founder. VPE/CTO
positions.description: Apple networking startup.  We made the "Gatorbox", a Macintosh to TCP/IP application gateway.  I was able to work with a lot of great people and we did great work together.  An excellent introduction to venture capital.

positions.title: Engineer
positions.description: Coin-op video game development on 68000 based cpu's in C.  Everyone was from MIT and we had a chef who cooked us lunch.  I met a lot of great people and learned an amazing amount in a short time.  I owe Keven and Doug a lot for that experience.
